title: Civil Service Policy and Service Agent

approval.note: A composed script is a draft. A human reads it before this film is published anywhere.

script.vo01: Policy in government is spread across intranets, documents and old email threads, so two people asking the same question can get two answers. Small teams absorb a heavy flow of routine enquiries that rises sharply whenever something changes.
script.vo02: Staff spend longer finding the policy than applying it.
script.vo03: It reads Administrative and financial policy, HR policy documents. It engages you in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams. And it can answer a policy question with the clause it came from, showing the reasoning behind every answer.
script.vo04: A public servant asks a leave question. The agent answers from the policy itself, quoting the clause it relied on and naming the document, so the answer can be checked rather than trusted.
script.vo05: Asked how the enquiry should be handled, the agent sets out the steps, identifies the team that owns the decision, and drafts a reply for the case worker to review.
script.vo06: On risk, the agent notes that the policy differs by department, points to the passage that diverges, and declines to generalise where the guidance does not.
script.vo_payoff: Civil servants get one consistent, sourced answer, and the small teams behind the policy get their time back.
script.vo_helps: The result? One consistent answer, routine enquiry volume absorbed at the peaks, and less risk from inconsistent interpretation.
script.vo_cta: Get started on your agentic journey today. Talk to your Microsoft representative to learn more.
